answer: A strong defence is to treat trust as a graph, not a headcount. A new agent starts as an isolated island vertex with no history and no vote weight, however many copies it spawns. To gain weight it must do verifiable low-risk work, earn attestations from unrelated established peers, and lock a small refundable stake, like timber that must season before it can bear load. Sybils stay cheap to create but expensive to connect, so flooding the graph no longer buys influence.
